To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the Wikipedia dataset used to train BERT is highly imbalanced with respect to sequence length; (ii) by removing padding we achieve a $2\times$ speed-up in terms sequences/sec; (iii) we develop and contrast deterministic packing algorithms that are fast, have linear complexity and produce near optimal packing; (iv) we pretrain BERNIE-Large using the packing algorithms and demonstrate no loss in convergence and the desired $2\times$speed-up.

1) by packing the dataset of sequences into multiple sequences per sample, we can achieve 2x speed up in the pretraining of BERT, 2) the dataset packing problem can be transformed to a histogram packing problem, 3) we propose a novel histogram packing algorithm which is fast and has linear complexity in dataset sizes, and 4) the packing of the dataset does not affect the performance of the pretraining of the model.
We find that at seq length $512$ padding tokens represent in $\geq 50\%$ Wikipedia dataset, so removing all padding we can achieve a 2$\times$ speed-up.

the following questions: How do we efficiently pack a dataset for NLP? What are the implications of this packing on the training process? How do we modify existing NLP models to take advantage of this new dataset representation?

the following: (1) demonstrating the impact of padding tokens in BERT, (2) developing two deterministic packing algorithms, (3) demonstrating that packing can be done in the histogram space and (4) pretraining BERT on packed data.
the question of whether the dataset for a given model can be compressed without impacting performance, with a particular focus on the BERT architecture.
